classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the signal distance as a chord, calculate a shorter side using the radius and perpendicular distance, then double it; the diagram supplies both equal half-chords.

content.prompt:
A shuttle bus travels along an isolated road.

The bus passes a cell tower 14 km away from a road.

The cell tower provides signal in a 31 km radius.

For how many kilometres will people on the bus have signal? Round your answer to 2 d.p.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8, signal circle and vertical road below the stem
spec.description: Signal circle centred at a labelled tower location; unfilled vertical road with a dashed centre line; dashed upper and lower radii, perpendicular distance and two half-chord labels.
spec.mathematics: Coverage radius 31 km and perpendicular tower-to-road distance 14 km. Both half-chord lengths are x. Drawing units use a uniform factor of 1/10; intersections are derived from the circle equation.
spec.answerVisibility: 31 km, 14 km and both x km labels are visible. The calculated half-chord and total distance are absent.

answer.worked:
$x$ is half the length of road within signal range.

$$\begin{align*}x&=\sqrt{31^2-14^2}\\x&=\sqrt{765}\text{ km}\\\text{Total distance}&=2\sqrt{765}\text{ km}\\\text{Total distance}&\approx55.32\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
